Legen or Liegen? German B1 Placement Practice

Choose legen for placing something down and liegen for its position. Practise the object and location clues in complete sentences.

B1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the difference

Legen describes putting an object down or into a lying position: Sie legt die Decke auf das Bett. Liegen describes where something lies: Die Decke liegt auf dem Bett. The person doing the placing is the subject of legen; the positioned item is the subject of liegen.

Common mistake to avoid

Do not use liegen as though it were the act of placing a direct object. Ich lege das Handy hin, but Das Handy liegt dort.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Sie legt die Decke auf das Bett.She puts the blanket on the bed.
Worked example 2Die Decke liegt auf dem Bett.The blanket lies on the bed.
Worked example 3Ich lege die Quittung in die Schublade.I put the receipt in the drawer.
Worked example 4Die Quittung liegt in der Schublade.The receipt is in the drawer.

Practice: choose the right word

Choose legen for placing an object down or liegen for describing its position; conjugate in the present or requested imperative. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. ___ die Zeitung bitte auf den Sessel! (place, du)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: Leg

The du imperative of legen is leg; lege is also possible.

Question 2. Die Zeitung ___ auf dem Sessel. (position)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: liegt

The newspaper is the subject of the position verb liegen.

Question 3. Wir ___ die Handtücher ins Regal. (place)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: legen

The subject puts the towels somewhere, so use legen.

Question 4. Wo ___ deine Handschuhe? (position)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: liegen

The plural subject takes liegen.

Revise it so it sticks

Return to this lesson tomorrow and complete the four gaps without looking at the rule. Then write two of your own sentences using today's pattern. Check whether the subject, case and verb position match the explanation.
